title: Speeding Costs More, Saves Just 54 Seconds — Study
paragraphs: Many drivers go faster than the speed limit because they want to save time. However, a new study from the United States says that speeding saves very little time but costs a lot of money.

The study was carried out by researchers at the University of Minnesota, and it was published in July 2026 in the journal Communications Sustainability. The researchers looked at about 120 million car trips across the US. The data came from four days in 2021, and the study included roads with speed limits of 45 miles per hour or more.
The researchers found that more than 43% of trips included speeding at least once. Drivers also spent almost 12% of their driving time above the speed limit.

But how much time did speeding save? According to the study, the average driver travels about 28.6 miles a day. If they followed the speed limit, their trips would take only about 54 seconds longer each day.

On the other hand, if all gasoline cars followed the speed limit, Americans could save about 6.7 million gallons of fuel every day. This would also save about $22 million a day, based on 2021 prices, and reduce carbon dioxide pollution. William Northrop, one of the researchers, said that driving slower is also better for electric cars.
However, another expert said that the fuel savings are only a small part of all the gasoline used in the US every day. The researchers also said that slower driving could change traffic patterns.
